report:
Comments on a note now work. `yarn verify` passes (144 tests) and the work is committed on the current branch as `ba9cc20`; nothing was pushed.

- **Commenting:** `POST /v1/notes/{id}/comments` with `{ text }` answers 202, and the outcome's result is the comment id. The note's owner and the accounts it is shared with can comment.
  - A missing, empty or blank text, a text over 500 characters, or a text that isn't a string is refused as `VALIDATION`.
  - An archived note is refused as `CONFLICT`, and so is a comment from an account it is shared with. Once the note is restored it takes comments again.
  - Someone who can't read the note, or a note that doesn't exist, gets `NOT_FOUND`. An anonymous caller gets 403.
- **Listing:** `GET /v1/notes/{id}/comments` answers 200 with `[{ id, authorId, text, createdAt }]`, oldest first. It answers 404 to anyone who can't read the note and 403 to an anonymous caller. Comments on an archived note can still be read.

The code is in `src/notes/notes.ts` and `src/notes/routes.ts`, with tests in `src/notes/comments.spec.ts`.

Where the spec was unclear, I decided:
- **Blank text:** a text of only spaces counts as missing, the same rule note titles follow.
- **Length:** the 500-character limit counts characters as people see them (code points), as titles do.
- **Error order:** a person who can't read the note gets `NOT_FOUND` first, then the text is checked, then whether the note is archived. This is the order reminders already use.
- **Editing and deleting:** there is no way to edit or delete a comment, because the feature doesn't ask for one.
- **Losing access:** the app has no way to unshare a note yet. Access is checked on every request, so if unsharing is added later, an account that loses access also loses its comments view.

A note's history now works. `yarn verify` passes (159 tests) and the work is committed on the current branch as `31c69f3`; nothing was pushed.

- **Versions:** each edit of a note, and each restore, keeps the title and text it replaces as the next numbered version. The time it was replaced is recorded as `replacedAt`. An edit that is refused keeps nothing.
- **Listing:** `GET /v1/notes/{id}/versions` answers the owner with `[{ version, title, text, replacedAt }]`, most recent first. This also works on archived notes. It answers 404 to anyone who isn't the owner and for a note that doesn't exist, and 403 to an anonymous caller.
- **Restoring:** `POST /v1/notes/{id}/versions/{version}/restore` answers 202. The chosen version becomes the note's content, and the content it replaced becomes a new version.
  - A version that doesn't exist (`0`, `-1`, `1.0`, `abc`, or a number past the last version) is refused as `NOT_FOUND`.
  - An archived note is refused as `CONFLICT`.

The code is in `src/notes/notes.ts` and `src/notes/routes.ts`, with tests in `src/notes/versions.spec.ts`.

Where the spec was unclear, I decided:
- **What gets listed:** only replaced content counts as a version, so a note that has never been edited lists `[]`. Version 1 is therefore the content as first written, once an edit has replaced it.
- **Refusal codes for restoring:** an account the note is shared with gets `FORBIDDEN`. Anyone else gets `NOT_FOUND`, as for every other owner-only change. Listing answers 404 to both, as the spec says.
- **Order of checks for restoring:** a version that doesn't exist is reported before an archived note.
- **Unchanged edits:** an edit that doesn't change the content still adds a version, since the spec says every edit does.
- **Restoring the current content:** there is no way to do this, because the current content is not itself a version.

Editors now work. `yarn verify` passes (178 tests) and the work is committed on the current branch as `2798b40`; nothing was pushed.

- **Sharing with a role:** `POST /v1/notes/{id}/share` takes an optional `role`, either `'reader'` (the default) or `'editor'`. Any other value, including `null`, is refused as `VALIDATION`.
  - Sharing again with the same account now succeeds and sets its role; it used to be refused. The account stays in `sharedWith` once, in its original position.
- **What an editor can do:** edit the title and text, list versions, restore a version, and comment.
- **What an editor can't do:** archive or restore the note, pin, unpin, tag, untag, share, or set a reminder. Each of these is refused as `FORBIDDEN`.
- **Owner's view:** the owner's view of a note, in both `GET /notes/{id}` and `GET /notes`, now includes `editors`. Editors are also listed in `sharedWith`. Nobody else sees `editors`.
- **Versions:** each version now has `editedBy`, the account whose edit or restore replaced it.

One existing test changed: the one that expected sharing again to be refused now expects it to succeed. Most of the code is in `src/notes/notes.ts`, with tests in `src/notes/editors.spec.ts`.

Where the spec was unclear, I decided:
- **Sharing again without a role:** this makes an editor a reader again, because the role defaults to `reader`.
- **Sharing again with the same role:** this succeeds and changes nothing.
- **Archived notes:** the role on an archived note can't be changed (`CONFLICT`), the same as sharing an archived note.
- **A reader editing:** a reader who tries to edit or restore a version gets `FORBIDDEN`. A reader listing versions gets 404, the same as a stranger.
- **Order in `editors`:** accounts appear in the order they became editors. An account made a reader and later an editor again goes to the end.

A signed-in person can now delete their own account with `DELETE /v1/accounts/me`. `yarn verify` passes (188 tests) and the work is committed on the current branch as `9eb0e04`; nothing was pushed.

- **The request:** it answers 202, or 403 to an anonymous caller.
- **Tokens and login:** every token the account held now makes requests anonymous, so `GET /accounts/me` with one answers 403. Logging in with the account's email answers 401.
- **Signing up again:** the email can sign up again and gets a new account id with no notes, no notifications and the Free plan.
- **Their notes:** the account's notes are deleted with their comments, versions, shares and any reminder still to come. The people a note was shared with get 404 for it, and it leaves their `GET /notes/shared` list.
- **Other people's notes:** the account is removed from `sharedWith` and `editors`, and its comments there are deleted.
- **Notifications and plan:** the account's notifications, including reminders not yet due, are deleted, and so is its plan.

The code is spread across the accounts, notes, notifications and plans modules, with tests in `src/accounts/deletion.spec.ts`.

Where the spec was unclear, I decided:
- **Versions on other people's notes:** versions the account's edits replaced stay on those notes, with `editedBy` still naming the deleted account id. Removing them would rewrite the owner's history, which the previous feature says is never lost.
- **Notifications others received:** an "archived" notification someone already got about a deleted owner's note stays with them, since it is theirs.
- **The delete outcome:** nobody can read it afterwards. It was issued by the account, and its token is now anonymous, so the tracker answers 404.

One test is weaker than it looks: the unit test that a deleted account's future reminders are forgotten runs on a fixed clock, so it never reaches the moment they would have fired. Over HTTP a re-signup gets a new account id, so the old account's reminders can't be observed that way either.

Search now works through `GET /v1/notes/search?q=…`. `yarn verify` passes (199 tests) and the work is committed on the current branch as `19185e6`; nothing was pushed.

- **What it searches:** the caller's own notes and the notes shared with them, leaving out archived ones. A restored note can be found again.
- **What matches:** a note matches when every word of the query appears in its title or its text, ignoring case.
- **Results:** `[{ id, title, ownerId }]`, most recent first.
- **Refusals:** a missing, empty or blank `q` gets 400. An anonymous caller gets 403.

The code is in `src/notes/notes.ts` and `src/notes/routes.ts`, with tests in `src/notes/search.spec.ts`.

Where the spec was unclear, I decided:
- **Words across fields:** each word can be in either field, so "trip train" matches a note titled "Trip…" whose text says "…train".
- **Parts of words:** a word matches anywhere inside a longer word, as "contains" says, so "grocer" finds "Groceries".
- **Splitting the query:** words are split on whitespace and extra spaces are ignored. Punctuation is matched literally.
- **What is searched:** only the current title and text. Comments, tags and old versions are not searched.
- **Repeated `q`:** a query with `q` given more than once (`?q=a&q=b`) gets 400.
